topic.title: Open Analyze Get Started
topic.text: Open the Analyze Get Started walkthrough. It guides you from choosing a image through calibration, detection, review, transfer, saving, and sharing. Audio starts with the first file and stops after the last. Select the launcher again to close it.

topic.text: Turn Explorer on to select a image-analysis control or area and hear what it does. Turn Explorer off when you want to edit the image, corners, or detected balls.

topic.title: Close Analyze page
topic.text: Close Analyze and return to the trainer table. Use Apply to Trainer Table first if you want to transfer the reviewed ball arrangement.
topic.summary: Close Analyze and return to the trainer table.

topic.title: Choose image
topic.text: Choose an image from this device. Portrait and landscape images keep their original proportions. Identify the head or kitchen end and the foot or rack end of the table. Then select Find / Add Corners to match the numbered reference points in the table diagram to your image.
topic.summary: Choose an image from this device.

topic.title: Corner sensing
topic.text: Corner Sensing estimates the four inside playing-surface corners in a full-table image. It orders them along the table’s long direction, including portrait images. Check the numbered diagram against the image and confirm the head and foot ends. Drag a marker to correct its position. If the orientation is wrong, select Reset Corners and use Find / Add Corners to mark the references yourself. For a partial table, choose its coverage in Custom Table Layouts and mark the highlighted points manually.
topic.summary: Corner Sensing estimates the four inside playing-surface corners in a full-table image.

topic.title: Custom Table Layouts
topic.text: Custom Table Layouts opens the table-region and alignment controls beside your image. The diagram follows the image’s estimated orientation. Use the Head / Kitchen End menu to choose its direction, or Flip Ends if the head and foot ends are reversed. Choose the coverage you can see and match the numbered references. Analyze Balls closes this panel so the right side shows the detected balls. Select Custom Table Layouts to open it again.
topic.summary: Custom Table Layouts opens the table-region and alignment controls beside your image.

topic.title: Reset corners
topic.text: Reset Corners clears the marked corners and their alignment references. Select Find / Add Corners to start marking again. Follow the highlighted numbered points in the table diagram, rather than the corners of your screen. For partial coverage, use the matching region boundaries, which may be diamond intersections instead of pockets.
topic.summary: Reset Corners clears the marked corners and their alignment references.

topic.title: Choose analysis rack type

topic.title: Analyze Balls
topic.text: Analyze Balls detects ball candidates inside the calibrated table region. Custom Table Layouts closes so you can review the detected balls on the right. Check each candidate and assign its identity before applying the layout to the Trainer.
topic.summary: Analyze Balls detects ball candidates inside the calibrated table region.

topic.title: Practice pathway
topic.summary: Start with cue ball speed and contact, then target landing, pattern play, and kick routes.
topic.text: Start with cue ball speed and contact, then target landing, pattern play, and kick routes. Finish with a scored benchmark. Open More for the matching video. Watch the creator demonstrate the layout, then build your own practice table. Save a starting layout before changing it so you can repeat the same test. Count pocketing, cue ball position, and legal contact separately. Your score should show what improved and what still needs work.

practice.Goal: Build accuracy, position, and recovery in a consistent order.
practice.Measure: Record a baseline score before making the drill harder.
practice.Trainer: Use Save Table File to keep or share the starting layout.

topic.title: Speed and contact baseline
topic.summary: Begin with a straight shot and center cue tip contact.
topic.text: Begin with a straight shot and center cue tip contact. Find the speed that produces a stop shot, then move the contact point higher for follow and lower for draw. Keep the object ball and pocket fixed while changing one setting at a time. Next, use a cut shot to compare the tangent line with the cue ball route. Before each shot, name the landing point you expect. Repeat each setup five times and record whether the cue ball finished short, long, left, or right.

practice.Goal: Separate aim errors from cue ball control errors.
practice.Setup: One object ball, one pocket, and a repeatable cue ball starting point.
practice.Measure: Repeat each setting five times and identify the direction of the miss.
practice.Trainer: Use cue tip contact, shot speed, tangent line, and Undo Last Shot.

topic.title: Target landing precision
topic.summary: Set up a repeatable object ball shot and choose a small cue ball landing zone.
topic.text: Set up a repeatable object ball shot and choose a small cue ball landing zone. Begin with a generous target, then reduce it as your control improves. For this practice plan, use a three inch target and count a success only when the object ball is pocketed and the cue ball center finishes inside the target. Shoot ten attempts. Change only speed, then contact height, then the cut angle. Aim for eight successes out of ten before making the target smaller. Open More for Dr. Dave’s target practice demonstration.

practice.Goal: Control the cue ball stopping point after pocketing.
practice.Setup: Use a three inch target, starting with an easier size if needed.
practice.Measure: Pocket the ball and land the cue ball center inside the target on 8 of 10 attempts.
practice.Trainer: Use a table marker for the landing zone; save the layout and use Undo to repeat it.

topic.title: Rock Around the Clock
topic.summary: Open More and use Niels Feijen’s demonstration to set up Rock Around the Clock.
topic.text: Open More and use Niels Feijen’s demonstration to set up Rock Around the Clock. Save the starting layout. Before every shot, choose the next object ball, its pocket, and the cue ball landing zone that leaves a useful angle. Prefer a route with room for a small speed error. Track pocketing and position separately. Complete one rotation first, then work toward three consecutive rotations without disturbing another ball. When you miss position, repeat the previous shot and compare a simpler route before changing the whole pattern.

practice.Goal: Plan the next shot before shooting the current one.
practice.Setup: Use the linked demonstration for the creator’s ball layout and sequence.
practice.Measure: For this plan, complete 3 consecutive rotations without disturbing a secondary ball.
practice.Trainer: Use Shot 2 to preview the next shot and Undo Last Shot to revisit a position error.

topic.title: One-rail kick reference
topic.summary: Place an object ball behind a blocker so the cue ball needs one cushion to reach it.
topic.text: Place an object ball behind a blocker so the cue ball needs one cushion to reach it. Open More for the diamond system tutorial. Identify the cue ball start, the rail aim point, and the intended object ball contact. Keep speed and spin consistent while testing the route. Repeat five attempts, moving the rail aim point by a small amount when the contact misses. Record the adjustment that works, then test a second starting location. Count legal object ball contact according to the game you are practicing.

practice.Goal: Build a reliable diamond reference before adding rails.
practice.Setup: One blocker, one target object ball, and a clear one-rail route.
practice.Measure: Make legal target contact on at least 4 of 5 attempts from each tested start.
practice.Trainer: Use the kick tool, diamonds, and a saved layout to compare aim points.

resources.title: Diamond System Formula — Kick Shots (Cue Craft Pro)

topic.title: Two-rail kick extension
topic.summary: Begin with a two cushion route that has space for the cue ball to travel.
topic.text: Begin with a two cushion route that has space for the cue ball to travel. Mark the first rail aim point and predict the second rail contact before shooting. Keep the same speed and spin for each attempt. If the first contact is wrong, adjust the aim point. If the first contact is right but the final contact misses, examine the second rail route and speed. Record five attempts from the same start, then move the cue ball to a new starting diamond. Open More for the linked kick reference.

practice.Goal: Extend a calibrated route to a second cushion.
practice.Setup: Choose a repeatable two-rail route with no unintended ball contact.
practice.Measure: Make legal target contact on at least 4 of 5 attempts before moving the starting point.
practice.Trainer: Use diamond and half-diamond references and compare the two rail contact points.

topic.title: Corner-5 three-rail route
topic.summary: Open More for Dr.
topic.text: Open More for Dr. Dave’s Corner-5 demonstration. Follow its starting, aiming, and arrival number scales together. Identify all three cushion contacts before you shoot. Start with a clear route, consistent speed, and the spin shown in the lesson. Compare the predicted arrival with the actual arrival, then make a small adjustment and repeat. Once the route is calibrated, add a target object ball and a blocker for escape practice. Test five different starting positions and record legal object ball contact separately from the final cue ball position.

practice.Goal: Use one consistent numbering system for a three-rail route.
practice.Setup: Use the linked lesson for the Corner-5 numbering and reference route.
practice.Measure: For this plan, make legal target contact on 4 of 5 selected escape attempts.
practice.Trainer: Mark rail references on the Trainer; record the adjustment for each start.

topic.title: Progressive difficulty benchmark
topic.summary: Open More for Sharivari’s progressive difficulty drill and use the demonstrated setup.
topic.text: Open More for Sharivari’s progressive difficulty drill and use the demonstrated setup. Save the starting layout and record your first score. For your Trainer adaptation, begin with a comfortable position zone. After a successful set, reduce the zone or increase the shot difficulty, changing one condition at a time. Count both the pocketed ball and the required cue ball position. If the same error repeats, return to the last successful level. Record the highest level you can repeat, rather than only your best isolated attempt.

practice.Goal: Increase difficulty only after a repeatable result.
practice.Setup: Use the linked demonstration, then define your Trainer target zone.
practice.Measure: Complete a repeatable successful set before reducing the margin.
practice.Trainer: Save one layout per difficulty level, with the level included in its name.

topic.title: 105-minute practice session
topic.summary: Use this one hundred and five minute practice plan.
topic.text: Use this one hundred and five minute practice plan. Spend thirty minutes on speed and target landing, aiming for eight successful pocket and position results out of ten with a three inch target. Spend forty five minutes on Rock Around the Clock, first completing one rotation and then working toward three consecutive rotations without disturbing another ball. Spend thirty minutes on kick escapes, starting with one rail and adding two and three rails as control improves. Test five selected escapes and aim for four legal contacts. Record the result at the end of each phase. If time runs out, save your layout and score, then continue there next session.

practice.Goal: Follow a measurable three-phase practice plan.
practice.Setup: 30 minutes target landing; 45 minutes pattern play; 30 minutes kick escapes.
practice.Measure: Targets are goals for this Trainer plan, not prerequisites or creator certification.
practice.Trainer: Name saved layouts by phase and difficulty so the next session starts in the same place.

topic.title: Review, save, and repeat
topic.summary: At the end of practice, record attempts, pocketed balls, successful position results, and legal kick contacts.
topic.text: At the end of practice, record attempts, pocketed balls, successful position results, and legal kick contacts. Note the most common miss and the single adjustment that helped. topic.title: Stop Shot Calibration
topic.text: Stop Shot Calibration. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot end. Place the 1-ball on the center spot. Put the cue ball on the head string, one diamond from the left long rail. This lines up with the foot-right corner pocket. Center a three-inch white circle one ball width behind the 1-ball, toward the cue ball. That is the cue ball’s stopping position. Use no side spin. Start slightly below center and adjust your speed and tip height until the cue ball arrives without forward or backward roll. Pocket the 1-ball and stop the cue ball inside the white circle. Reset both balls after each attempt. Try five shots and count clean stops. In the Trainer, select Execute Shot to watch the result.
topic.summary: Stop Shot Calibration.

topic.title: 90-Degree Stun Tangent Line
topic.text: Ninety-Degree Stun Tangent Line. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball one diamond inward from the right side pocket. Put the cue ball on the table’s center line, half a diamond toward the foot end from the center spot. Place a three-inch yellow square one and a half diamonds toward the head end from the 1-ball, and one ball width to its left. Pocket the 1-ball into the right side pocket. Use no side spin and enough low tip contact and speed for the cue ball to be sliding at impact. It should leave along the tangent line, perpendicular to the object ball’s path. Adjust speed to finish inside the yellow square. Reset both balls and repeat five times. Select Execute Shot in the Trainer to compare the path with the tangent line.

topic.title: Speed Ladder — Four Zones
topic.text: Speed Ladder. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Use only the cue ball. Start on the center line, half a diamond behind the head string. Place four three-inch circles on the center line: white on the center spot, red on the foot spot, yellow one diamond from the foot cushion, and pink one diamond from the head cushion. Reset the cue ball to the same starting position before every shot. First, stop on white. Second, stop on red. Third, touch the foot cushion and return to yellow. Fourth, touch the foot cushion and return all the way to pink. Use a level cue and no side spin. Change your stroke speed while keeping your delivery smooth. Score one point for each finish inside its circle, for a maximum of four. Repeat the ladder and compare your scores.

topic.title: L-Drill — Five-Ball Rotation
topic.text: The L-Drill. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place balls one, two, and three half a diamond from the right long rail, respectively one, two, and three diamonds from the foot cushion. Place ball four one diamond from the right long rail and half a diamond from the foot cushion. Place ball five on the center line, also half a diamond from the foot cushion. These five balls form an L. Put a white square at the center spot, one diamond wide. Start the cue ball on the center line, half a diamond behind the head string. Pocket balls one through five in order, choosing clear corner pockets. Plan the next angle before every shot. Use the center square as a recovery option when it helps the next shot. Count balls pocketed in sequence, then reset the full pattern and try again.

topic.title: T-Drill — Center and Foot String
topic.text: The T-Drill. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place ball one on the center spot. Place ball two one diamond farther toward the foot, and ball three on the foot spot. Put ball four on the foot string, one diamond to the left of ball three, and ball five one diamond to its right. Start the cue ball on the head string, one diamond from the right long rail. Place two yellow circles, each half a diamond wide, halfway between the center spot and the side pockets. Pocket balls one through five in order into corner pockets. Choose the yellow zone that gives you a useful angle for the next ball. Use a cushion when it helps the route. Keep the cue ball clear of the remaining balls. Count your run, reset the full pattern, and work toward completing all five.
topic.summary: The T-Drill.

topic.title: Wagon Wheel — Six Target Zones
topic.text: The Wagon Wheel. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball one diamond inward from the right side pocket. Put the cue ball on the center line, half a diamond toward the foot from the center spot. Set six three-inch circles on the head side of the 1-ball. Marker one is one and a half diamonds from the left rail and three and a half from the head rail. Marker two is two from the left and three from the head. Marker three is one ball width left of the 1-ball’s line and three from the head. Marker four is three and a quarter from the left and three from the head. Marker five is three and a half from the left and two and a half from the head. Marker six is directly headward of marker three, one and a half diamonds from the head rail. Reset both balls before every attempt and pocket the 1-ball into the right side pocket. Work through the markers in order, varying draw, follow, and speed. Start without side spin. Record the combinations that produce repeatable finishes.
topic.summary: The Wagon Wheel.

topic.title: Two-Rail Center Recovery
topic.text: Two-Rail Center Recovery. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball one diamond from the right long rail and one diamond from the foot cushion. Put the cue ball on the same rail offset, three diamonds from the foot cushion. Place a white square on the center line, one diamond from the head cushion. Make the square one diamond wide. Pocket the 1-ball into the foot-right corner. Start with natural forward roll and no side spin. Look for the cue ball to contact the foot cushion, then the left long cushion, and travel toward the white recovery zone. Adjust your stroke speed to finish in the square. Keep the ball placements fixed so you can compare attempts. Score the pocketed ball and the position result separately. Try five shots, then repeat your most successful speed.

topic.title: Side Pocket Scratch Avoidance
topic.text: Side Pocket Scratch Avoidance. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball half a diamond inward from the right side pocket. Start the cue ball on the foot spot. Place a red square beside the head-right corner pocket, centered a quarter diamond from each cushion. Make it half a diamond wide. Place a white square on the center line, one diamond from the foot cushion, and make it one diamond wide. Pocket the 1-ball into the right side pocket. Compare forward roll, stun, and controlled draw, starting without side spin. Watch the whole cue ball route, including any cushion rebounds. Find a stroke that keeps the cue ball clear of the red danger zone and returns it toward white. In the Trainer, judge whether the path enters the red zone, even if cue ball pocketing is prevented. Reset both balls and repeat five times.
topic.summary: Side Pocket Scratch Avoidance.

topic.title: One-Rail Mirror Kick
topic.text: One-Rail Mirror Kick. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Put the cue ball on the head string, one diamond from the right long rail. Place the 1-ball on that same line, three diamonds from the foot cushion. Put the 8-ball halfway between them to block the direct shot. The cue ball and the 1-ball are now equally distant from the left cushion. Mark the left cushion halfway between their lengthwise positions: three and a half diamonds from the head cushion. Center a yellow circle one ball radius inside that cushion as the cue ball contact reference. Use a level cue, moderate speed, and no side spin. Send the cue ball to the left cushion, then into the 1-ball without touching the 8-ball first. Begin with the midpoint reference and make small aiming adjustments from your observed results. Reset the cue ball after each attempt and count five clean contacts.
topic.summary: One-Rail Mirror Kick.

topic.title: Two-Rail Corner Kick
topic.text: Two-Rail Corner Kick. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the cue ball one diamond from the head cushion and one and a quarter diamonds from the right long rail. Put the 1-ball one diamond from the foot cushion and three quarters of a diamond from the right long rail. Place the 8-ball level with the side pockets, one diamond from the right rail. Put balls two and three on the same line, two ball widths to either side of the 8-ball toward the head and foot ends. This blocks the direct shot. Place yellow marker A at the right cushion on the foot string, with its center one ball radius inside the cloth. Place yellow marker B half a diamond left of the foot-right corner, also one ball radius inside the foot cushion. Use moderate speed and no side spin. Aim the cue ball center toward A. Look for right cushion, then foot cushion near B, then contact with the 1-ball. Make small aiming adjustments and count five successful escapes.
topic.summary: Two-Rail Corner Kick.

topic.title: Find / Add Corners
topic.text: Find / Add Corners opens the numbered table diagram for manual marking. Match the highlighted reference to the same point in your image and tap it. Continue through all four references. Portrait and landscape images use the same table references, even though they appear in different places on the screen. If four corners are already marked, drag their markers to adjust them, or use Reset Corners to start again.
topic.summary: Find / Add Corners opens the numbered table diagram for manual marking.

topic.title: Set the table corners
topic.text: After choosing an image, select Find / Add Corners. The small table diagram highlights the next point to mark. Match that point to the same physical corner or boundary in your image. For a full table, start at the head-end corner shown as pocket one. Follow the same long rail to pocket three at the foot end. Cross the foot-end short rail to pocket four, then return along the other long rail to pocket six. This table-based order works for portrait and landscape images; the first two points follow a long rail, rather than the top edge of the screen. Use Reset Corners if you need to begin again. Use Custom Table Layouts for partial coverage and diamond references. Corner Sensing can estimate a full-table outline, but check its numbered orientation before continuing. Once the outline matches, select Analyze Balls.
topic.summary: After choosing an image, select Find / Add Corners.

topic.title: Head / Kitchen End
topic.text: The Head / Kitchen End menu controls how the table diagram matches your image. Auto estimates portrait or landscape orientation from the image and corner outline. It cannot identify the actual head end from the cloth alone. Choose Top or Bottom for a vertical table, or Left or Right for a horizontal table. Match the head, break, and kitchen end to the real table. Changing orientation clears the previous ball analysis so you can check the corners and analyze again.
topic.summary: The Head / Kitchen End menu controls how the table diagram matches your image.

topic.title: Flip Ends
topic.text: Flip Ends swaps the head and foot ends of the table diagram. Use it when the head, break, or kitchen end is shown at the opposite end from your image. Existing corner positions stay in place, but their numbered table references change. Review the alignment and select Analyze Balls again.
topic.summary: Flip Ends swaps the head and foot ends of the table diagram.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Choose an image
topic.text: Tap Choose Image to begin. You can also open a saved image, load a saved table file, or use the current image. Back revisits a step. Next confirms choices. The walkthrough waits for required actions.
topic.summary: Tap Choose Image to begin.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Select and open
topic.text: Select your image and choose Open in the device window. For a saved image, select its name and tap Open. For a table file, select the file and open it. We will continue when it has loaded.
topic.summary: Select your image and choose Open in the device window.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Open corner setup
topic.text: Your image is loaded. Tap Find / Add Corners to open the table diagram. For a partial table image, choose the matching coverage in Custom Table Layouts before marking the corners.
topic.summary: Your image is loaded.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Identify four corners
topic.text: Match each highlighted numbered reference on the diagram to the inside cushion edge in your image. Notice the orientation: Top or Bottom is portrait; Left or Right is landscape. For a full table in Auto, pocket one becomes top right in portrait and top left in landscape. Corner Sensing can estimate a full-table outline. Check all four markers.
topic.summary: Match each highlighted numbered reference on the diagram to the inside cushion edge in your image.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Confirm orientation
topic.text: Check the head, break, and kitchen end against your image. Choose Top or Bottom for portrait, or Left or Right for landscape. Use Flip Ends if reversed. Check the foot spot message and the four numbered markers. Tap Next when the orientation and alignment are correct.
topic.summary: Check the head, break, and kitchen end against your image.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Confirm rack type
topic.text: Leave Rack on Auto, or select the game shown in your image. Use Custom for a drill or an unusual arrangement. Select a different rack type, or tap Next to keep the current choice.
topic.summary: Leave Rack on Auto, or select the game shown in your image.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Analyze the balls
topic.text: Tap Analyze Balls. The walkthrough waits for analysis to finish. AI Ready shows the detector status; if the trained detector is unavailable, the app can use its local fallback.
topic.summary: Tap Analyze Balls.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Review every ball
topic.text: Check every ball number and position. Tap an image marker or ball icon to find its review entry. Correct identities and delete false detections. Add Missed Ball places one ball per activation. Zoom and pan to check closely. Tap Next when all remaining balls have unique identities and the layout looks right.
topic.summary: Check every ball number and position.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Keep an image or file?
topic.text: Saving here is optional. Save Image keeps the image on this device. Download saves an image copy. Save Table File downloads a shareable layout. These are separate from saving a named Trainer layout. Choose any you want, then tap Next, or simply tap Next to skip.
topic.summary: Saving here is optional.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Send the layout to Trainer
topic.text: Choose Apply to Trainer Table to practice now. Or enter a layout name and choose Apply plus Save Layout to keep it for reuse on this device. The walkthrough finishes only after the layout is successfully applied.
topic.summary: Choose Apply to Trainer Table to practice now.

topic.title: Walkthrough: Ready to practice
topic.text: Your reviewed layout is now on the Trainer table. If you chose Apply plus Save, the named layout is also saved on this device. You can now practice the arrangement.
topic.summary: Your reviewed layout is now on the Trainer table.

topic.title: Cue / Shaft Preset
topic.text: Cue and Shaft Preset is in Advanced Physics and Calibration. Standard shaft keeps the original squirt setting. Low-deflection shaft reduces squirt while keeping the same tip spin. Custom opens the cue ball to end-mass ratio for individual adjustment. The choice applies to both shots and is saved with your settings.
topic.summary: Cue and Shaft Preset is in Advanced Physics and Calibration.
